Complements MECHANISM_CUTTING_ACL_MECHANISM.md (the other canonical non-contact ACL mechanism) with the landing/jump mechanism, falsified via impulse-momentum + energy-balance physics rather than plane-of-loading.

pre_registration.C1_impulse_momentum: for FIXED touchdown momentum (fixed height), peak vGRF and loading rate are NOT fixed -- they scale with landing stiffness/technique (shorter effective deceleration time -> higher peak force), reproducible across >=2 independent decorrelated studies at matched height.
pre_registration.not_C1_adversary: peak GRF is a function of height/momentum ALONE; at matched height, technique/stiffness makes no measurable difference (non-significant or <15%).
pre_registration.C2_joint_redistribution: eccentric work absorbing touchdown momentum is shared across ankle+knee+hip, and the SHARE (not just total) shifts with stiffness -- hip+knee dominant when soft/flexed, ankle relatively more engaged when stiff/erect -- replicated across >=2 decorrelated labs/years.
pre_registration.not_C2_adversary: the per-joint percentage split is invariant to technique.
pre_registration.C3_dysfunction_pole: a stiff, extended-knee, valgus-collapsing landing loads the ACL more than a soft flexed neutral one, via (a) higher peak force/loading rate and (b) the knee sitting closer to this twin's own ligament model's most-taut angular range.
pre_registration.not_C3_adversary: landing kinetics are unrelated to the prospective ACL-injury literature's own measured group differences.
pre_registration.forced_adversary: 'landing force is fixed regardless of technique', forced to its strongest fair form as a SAME-HEIGHT (momentum-matched) multi-technique comparison, not a cross-height confound.
pre_registration.external_anchor_decorrelated_never_tauto: 9 primary sources (5 function-pole + 4 dysfunction-pole), all PMID/DOI live-verified this session via NCBI eutils, none tuned to or derived from this twin's own model.

velocity_crosscheck.source: Zhang, Bates & Dufek 2000 (PMID 10776901) -- reports BOTH heights and velocities used
velocity_crosscheck.verdict: all 3 within 0.4% -- free-fall model confirmed against numbers this twin did not choose

energy_balance_refinement.task_framing: total negative work = KE at touchdown (1/2 m v^2) -- an implicit Delta_y_crouch->0 approximation
energy_balance_refinement.refined_model: |W_eccentric| = 1/2 m v^2_touchdown + m g Delta_y_crouch -- ALWAYS >= 1/2 v^2 alone, not equal to it; predicts soft (large Delta_y) landings require MORE total muscle work than naive KE suggests, not just the same total redistributed
energy_balance_refinement.numeric_closure: NOT closed this session -- no fetched source reports Delta_y_crouch directly

measured_vs_KE_ratio.honest_caveat: ratio<100% is close to guaranteed regardless of measurement validity (since 1/2v^2 itself under-estimates true required work) -- limited discriminating power on its own; the FALLING-WITH-HEIGHT TREND is the more informative part, candidate causes (frontal/transverse-plane work, trunk/arm contribution, passive-tissue/SSC storage, incomplete stick) not resolved this pass

falsifier_tests.cite: Self & Paine 2001, Med Sci Sports Exerc

falsifier_tests.measured: peak vertical force and peak tibial acceleration HIGHEST for stiff-knee-heel technique: 2418 N, 20.7 G -- explicitly the highest-ranked of the 4 techniques at fixed height/momentum
falsifier_tests.verdict: PASS (not_C1 falls directly -- same mDeltav, different peak F)

falsifier_tests.cite: Zhang, Bates & Dufek 2000, Med Sci Sports Exerc
falsifier_tests.measured: general increases in peak GRF, peak joint moments, and powers with increases in landing height AND STIFFNESS (explicit, separate main effect)

falsifier_tests.cite: DeVita & Skelly 1992, Med Sci Sports Exerc
falsifier_tests.design: single 59cm drop, soft (>90deg knee flexion) vs stiff (<90deg) technique, 10 trials each, 8 female athletes
falsifier_tests.measured: soft 117deg vs stiff 77deg mean knee flexion; 'the stiff landing had larger GRFs' (direct quote; exact N/BW values are in the full-text table, not the fetched abstract -- disclosed gap)
falsifier_tests.verdict: PASS (qualitative direction confirmed; magnitude not extractable from abstract)

falsifier_tests.design: drop jumps from 20/30/40/50/60cm, DIRECTLY measured leg/knee/ankle stiffness
falsifier_tests.measured: peak vGRF EXCEEDED 3x body weight at 50/60cm (p<0.004 vs 20/30/40cm); leg/knee/ankle stiffness SIGNIFICANTLY LESS at 60cm than 20/30/40cm (p<0.037) -- endogenous stiffness modulation correlates with, is not epiphenomenal to, the force outcome

impulse_momentum_illustrative_model.model: half-sine contact pulse: F_peak = (pi/2) * m * v / T_contact, for fixed touchdown v (fixed height)
impulse_momentum_illustrative_model.caveat: illustrative T values, not measured -- shows direction/magnitude only, brackets the task's own ~3-6xBW framing as physically reasonable for intermediate T

decker2003_sex_based_strategy.reading: a THIRD independent manipulation (sex, not height or technique) reproducing the same proximal-vs-distal redistribution axis -- and mechanistically bridging to the dysfunction pole (erect/distally-shifted female strategy)
